title: Vakratuṇḍa Mahākāya
textOriginal:
वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय सूर्यकोटि समप्रभ ।
निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा ॥
transliteration:
vakratuṇḍa mahākāya sūryakoṭi samaprabha |
nirvighnaṃ kuru me deva sarvakāryeṣu sarvadā ||
meaning: O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty body, radiant as ten million suns: make all my undertakings free of obstacles, always.
sourceText: Traditional Gaṇeśa invocation verse (popular prayer; no single canonical scriptural locus identified in the sources)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. shlokam.org matches word for word (writes "sūryakoṭi samaprabha"). Variant: sanskritdocuments shloka1.html reads "कोटिसूर्यसमप्रभ" (same meaning, word order swapped).

title: Om Namaḥ Śivāya (Pañcākṣara)
textOriginal: ॐ नमः शिवाय
transliteration: oṃ namaḥ śivāya
meaning: "Om, salutation to Śiva" — the five-syllable (na-maḥ-śi-vā-ya) mantra of Śiva, with the sacred syllable Om.
sourceText: Pañcākṣara mantra; Vedic root in Śrī Rudram (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5.8, Rudram anuvāka 8): "namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca"
notes: "ॐ नमः शिवाय" copied from the mantra line in sanskritdocuments Rudra Panchakam. Vedic locus confirmed on sanskritdocuments Rudram (vinā-svara) at anuvāka 8.1: "नमः शिवाय च शिवतराय च" and in the svara-sahita Rudram (anuvāka 8). The Rudram line itself has no "ॐ"; the Om-prefixed five-syllable form is the traditional japa form. The Rudram nyāsa on the same page also says "नमः शिवायेति बीजम्". IAST generated mechanically from the Devanagari.

title: Karpūragauraṃ Karuṇāvatāraṃ
textOriginal:
कर्पूरगौरं करुणावतारं
संसारसारं भुजगेन्द्रहारम् ।
सदा वसन्तं हृदयारविन्दे
भवं भवानीसहितं नमामि ॥
transliteration:
karpūragauraṃ karuṇāvatāraṃ
saṃsārasāraṃ bhujagendrahāram |
sadā vasantaṃ hṛdayāravinde
bhavaṃ bhavānīsahitaṃ namāmi ||
meaning: I bow to Bhava (Śiva), white as camphor, compassion incarnate, the essence of worldly existence, garlanded with the king of serpents, ever dwelling in the lotus of the heart, together with Bhavānī.
sourceText: Traditional Śiva dhyāna/ārati verse (commonly said to be from the Yajurveda tradition; no canonical locus confirmed in the fetched sources)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. shlokam.org agrees (writes "संसारसारम्" and "सदावसन्तं" joined; same reading). Variant: sanskritdocuments Rudra Panchakam reads "सदा रमन्तं" ("always delighting") instead of "सदा वसन्तं" ("always dwelling"); the vasantaṃ reading is the one in both other sources. The source verse has a danda only after lines 2 and 4, reproduced as-is.

title: Śāntākāraṃ Bhujagaśayanaṃ
textOriginal:
शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं
विश्वाधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् ।
लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं
वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥
transliteration:
śāntākāraṃ bhujagaśayanaṃ padmanābhaṃ sureśaṃ
viśvādhāraṃ gaganasadṛśaṃ meghavarṇaṃ śubhāṅgam |
lakṣmīkāntaṃ kamalanayanaṃ yogibhirdhyānagamyaṃ
vande viṣṇuṃ bhavabhayaharaṃ sarvalokaikanātham ||
meaning: I worship Viṣṇu, the peaceful one who reclines on the serpent, lotus-navelled lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast as the sky, cloud-dark and beautiful of form; Lakṣmī's beloved, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation, remover of the fear of worldly existence, sole lord of all worlds.
sourceText: Viṣṇu dhyāna verse (recited as part of the Gītā-dhyāna / Gītā-māhātmya preliminaries)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Both check sources agree word for word; only orthographic differences (shloka3 writes "शुभांगम्" with anusvara; drikpanchang writes final "-म्" instead of anusvara, e.g. "शान्ताकारम् भुजगशयनम्"). No substantive variants.

title: Hare Kṛṣṇa Mahā-mantra
textOriginal:
हरे राम हरे राम राम राम हरे हरे ।
हरे कृष्ण हरे कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण हरे हरे ॥
transliteration:
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare |
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare ||
meaning: An invocation of the divine names Hari, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, sixteen names in all; the Upaniṣad teaches that chanting them removes the defects of the Kali age.
sourceText: Kali-Santaraṇa Upaniṣad (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda), section 2
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. The Upaniṣad gives the "Hare Rāma" half FIRST. Wikipedia confirms this order and notes that the popular order (Hare Kṛṣṇa first, as sung by ISKCON/Gauḍīya tradition following Caitanya) reverses the two lines. If the temple uses the popular order, swap the two lines; do not alter the words.

title: Śrī Rāma Rāma Rāmeti
textOriginal:
श्रीरामरामरामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
सहस्रनामतत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥
transliteration:
śrīrāmarāmarāmeti rame rāme manorame |
sahasranāmatattulyaṃ rāmanāma varānane ||
meaning: Śiva tells Pārvatī: "O fair-faced one, I delight in Rāma, the delightful, by repeating Rāma, Rāma; the one name of Rāma is equal to the thousand names (of Viṣṇu)."
sourceText: Viṣṇu Sahasranāma (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva), uttara-pīṭhikā / phala-śruti, verse 27 (Īśvara uvāca)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. stotranidhi (IAST) matches: "śrīrāma rāma rāmēti ramē rāmē manōramē | sahasranāma tattulyaṁ rāma nāma varānanē || 27 ||". Source prints an alternative reading "(रामरामेति रामेति)" for the first pāda, removed from the text and recorded here. Popular recitation often spaces it "श्रीराम राम रामेति".

title: Ugraṃ Vīraṃ Mahāviṣṇuṃ (Nṛsiṃha Mantrarāja)
textOriginal:
उग्रं वीरं महाविष्णुं
ज्वलन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् ।
नृसिंहं भीषणं भद्रं
मृत्युमृत्युं नमाम्यहम् ॥
transliteration:
ugraṃ vīraṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ
jvalantaṃ sarvatomukham |
nṛsiṃhaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhadraṃ
mṛtyumṛtyuṃ namāmyaham ||
meaning: I bow to Nṛsiṃha, the fierce and heroic Great Viṣṇu, blazing and facing every direction; terrifying yet auspicious, the death of Death itself.
sourceText: Nṛsiṃha Mantrarāja (anuṣṭubh), expounded pada by pada in the Nṛsiṃha Pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad (Atharvaveda)
notes: Devanagari copied from bhaktibharat (sanskritdocuments has no clean contiguous copy of the verse). Cross-checked word by word against the Nṛsiṃha-tāpanīya Upaniṣad on sanskritdocuments, which lists the eleven padas: उग्रं, वीरं, महाविष्णुं, ज्वलन्तं, सर्वतोमुखं, नृसिंहं, भीषणं, भद्रं, मृत्युमृत्युं, नमामि, अहम् — all match. Removed the leading "ॐ" printed on the source (a customary prefix, not part of the 32-syllable anuṣṭubh); add it back if the temple chants it. Variant: shlokam.org reads "मृत्योर् मृत्युं" (mṛtyor mṛtyuṃ, "death of death" as two words); the Upaniṣad has the compound "मृत्युमृत्युं", used here. IAST generated mechanically from the Devanagari.

title: Sarvamaṅgala Māṅgalye
textOriginal:
सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ।
शरण्ये त्र्यम्बके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
transliteration:
sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike |
śaraṇye tryambake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te ||
meaning: O auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, O gracious Śivā who fulfils every aim, O refuge, three-eyed Gaurī — Nārāyaṇī, salutations to you.
sourceText: Devī Māhātmyam (Durgā Saptaśatī, Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa) 11.10
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Source numbers it ॥ ११.१०॥. vignanam (verse 10) matches in substance: "sarva maṅgaḻa māṅgaḻyē śivē sarvārtha sādhikē। śaraṇyē trayambakē gaurī nārāyaṇi namō'stutē" — its "trayambakē"/"gaurī" are orthographic slips for tryambake/gauri; sanskritdocuments reading kept.

title: Yā Devī Sarvabhūteṣu Śaktirūpeṇa
textOriginal:
या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता ।
नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥
transliteration:
yā devī sarvabhūteṣu śaktirūpeṇa saṃsthitā |
namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
meaning: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings in the form of power (śakti): salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, again and again.
sourceText: Devī Māhātmyam (Durgā Saptaśatī) 5.32–34 (the śakti-rūpeṇa verse of the Aparājitā-stuti)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Source numbers it ॥ ५.३२-३४॥ (the refrain counts as three ślokas in the 700-verse count); vignanam numbers it 18 in its own count. Wording identical apart from a vignanam orthographic slip "sarvabhūtēṣū" (long ū). Do NOT use sanskritdocuments shloka1.html for this verse — it has typos ("शक्तिरुपेण संस्थितः").

title: Mahālakṣmyaṣṭakam, verse 1
textOriginal:
नमस्तेऽस्तु महामाये श्रीपीठे सुरपूजिते ।
शङ्खचक्रगदाहस्ते महालक्ष्मि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
transliteration:
namaste'stu mahāmāye śrīpīṭhe surapūjite |
śaṅkhacakragadāhaste mahālakṣmi namo'stu te ||
meaning: Salutations to you, O Great Māyā, seated on the throne of prosperity, worshipped by the gods; O Mahālakṣmī, holding conch, discus and mace, salutations to you.
sourceText: Mahālakṣmyaṣṭakam (spoken by Indra; traditionally assigned to the Padma Purāṇa), verse 1
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Source prefixes "इन्द्र उवाच ।" (Indra said), omitted from the verse. stotranidhi matches: "namastē:'stu mahāmāyē śrīpīṭhē surapūjitē | śaṅkhacakragadāhastē mahālakṣmi namō:'stu tē". The Padma Purāṇa attribution is traditional and was not confirmed in the fetched sources.

title: Om Śaravaṇabhava (Ṣaḍakṣara)
textOriginal: ॐ शरवणभव
transliteration: oṃ śaravaṇabhava
meaning: "Om, (salutation to) the one born in the Śaravaṇa reed-pond" — the six-syllable (śa-ra-va-ṇa-bha-va) mantra of Murugan/Skanda.
sourceText: Subrahmaṇya ṣaḍakṣara mantra (six-syllable mantra of Skanda/Murugan)
notes: "ॐ शरवणभव" copied from the sanskritdocuments Subrahmanya index entry "सुब्रह्मण्यषडशाक्षरमन्त्रः २ (ॐ शरवणभव)"; the linked document page itself returned 404 when fetched, so only the index title was verified. The Śaravaṇabhava Mantrākṣara Ṣaṭkam on sanskritdocuments devotes one verse to each syllable (श, र, व, न, भ, व) — note it spells the 4th syllable with dental न in its title and verse; the ṇ spelling (शरवणभव) is the one in the mantra entry and in Tamil "சரவணபவ". Tamil source (webdunia) calls "சரவணபவ" Murugan's ṣaḍakṣara (six-letter) mantra. Tamil-script form for display: "ஓம் சரவணபவ" (Om + the Tamil spelling from webdunia; the combined string was not found verbatim on a fetched page). IAST generated mechanically from the Devanagari.

title: Swāmiye Śaraṇam Ayyappa
textOriginal: സ്വാമിയേ ശരണമയ്യപ്പാ
transliteration: svāmiye śaraṇamayyappā
meaning: "O Lord Ayyappa, you are my refuge" — the surrender-call chanted by Sabarimala pilgrims.
sourceText: Śaraṇam-vili (pilgrim chant) of Sabarimala Ayyappa devotees; not a scriptural text
notes: Malayalam copied from Janmabhumi (body text: "സ്വാമിയേ ശരണമയ്യപ്പാ", described as the navākṣarī — nine-syllable — mantra among the śaraṇam calls); the article headline spells it without the final long ā ("ശരണമയ്യപ്പ"). Bhakthi Margam blog uses the same "ശരണമയ്യപ്പാ" spelling. Hinduism Today (1996) describes the chant in English as "Swamiye, Saranam Ayyappa". IAST generated mechanically (Malayalam->IAST); note Malayalam േ is long ē, rendered "e" by IAST convention. Chant, not scripture; no authorship/copyright issue.

title: Navagraha Stotram — Sūrya verse
textOriginal:
जपाकुसुमसंकाशं काश्यपेयं महाद्युतिम् ।
तमोऽरिं सर्वपापघ्नं प्रणतोऽस्मि दिवाकरम् ॥
transliteration:
japākusumasaṃkāśaṃ kāśyapeyaṃ mahādyutim |
tamo'riṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ praṇato'smi divākaram ||
meaning: I bow to the Sun, the maker of day, red as the hibiscus flower, son of Kaśyapa, of great brilliance, the enemy of darkness and destroyer of all sins.
sourceText: Navagraha Stotram (attributed to Vyāsa), verse 1 (Sūrya)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Both check sources match word for word (stotranidhi: "japākusumasaṅkāśaṁ kāśyapēyaṁ mahādyutim | tamō:'riṁ sarvapāpaghnaṁ praṇatō:'smi divākaram"). Source writes संकाशं with anusvara; saṅkāśaṃ is the same word.

title: Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva
textOriginal:
गङ्गे च यमुने चैव गोदावरि सरस्वति ।
नर्मदे सिन्धु कावेरि जलेऽस्मिन् संनिधिं कुरु ॥
transliteration:
gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati |
narmade sindhu kāveri jale'smin saṃnidhiṃ kuru ||
meaning: O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu and Kāverī — be present in this water.
sourceText: Snāna / jala-śuddhi (water-sanctifying) verse; identified by a Sanskrit scholar on the Bhāratīya Vidvat Pariṣat list as Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Brahma-khaṇḍa 26.66 (not independently verified)
notes: Devanagari copied from shlokam.org; the source prints no dandas, so "।" and "॥" were added at the half-verse and verse end (punctuation only). The bvparishat thread quotes the identical text "गङ्गे च यमुने चैव गोदावरि सरस्वति। नर्मदे सिन्धु कावेरि जलेऽस्मिन्सन्निधिं कुरु।" (read via summarising fetch, so treat as a secondary check). Common corrupt variant (joyfulslokas blog, many posters): "गोदावरी सरस्वती / नर्मदा ... कावेरी ... सन्निधम्" — these lose the vocative endings and should not be used. sanskritdocuments has no copy. IAST generated mechanically from the Devanagari.

title: Brahma-stuti by the Devas (Matsya Purāṇa), verse 1
textOriginal:
त्वमोङ्कारोऽस्यङ्कुराय प्रसूतो विश्वस्यात्मानन्तभेदस्य पूर्वम् ।
सम्भूतस्यानन्तरं सत्त्वमूर्ते संहारेच्छोस्ते नमो रुद्रमूर्त्ते ॥
transliteration:
tvamoṅkāro'syaṅkurāya prasūto viśvasyātmānantabhedasya pūrvam |
sambhūtasyānantaraṃ sattvamūrte saṃhārecchoste namo rudramūrtte ||
meaning: You are Om, born first as the sprout of the universe with its endless variety; after creation you take a form of sattva to sustain it, and when you will its dissolution you are Rudra — salutations to you.
sourceText: Matsya Purāṇa 154.7 (Devakṛtā Brahmastuti, ślokas 154.7–15), verse 1
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. Chosen because it is a hymn addressed to Brahmā with a stated Purāṇic locus. Sanskrit Wikisource (मत्स्यपुराणम्/अध्यायः १५४, v. 154.7) differs in two places: "सत्वमूर्ते" (vs "सत्त्वमूर्ते") and "संहारेच्छास्ते" (vs "संहारेच्छोस्ते"); the sanskritdocuments readings are the grammatically regular ones and were kept. Content caveat: this verse praises Brahmā as the one source who also acts as Rudra in dissolution — suitable for a Brahmā entry, but it is not a short popular dhyāna; review before display.

title: Om Sai Ram
textOriginal: Om Sai Ram
transliteration: Om Sai Ram
transliterationScheme: source romanization (no Devanagari form found on a fetched page)
meaning: A devotional name-chant: "Om" joined with the name of Sai Baba and of Rāma, used by devotees as japa and as a greeting.
sourceText: Devotional chant / greeting of Sai Baba devotees (not scripture)
notes: Chant, not scripture. Sources describe "Om Sai Ram" / "Aum Sai Ram" as a chant and greeting among Shirdi Sai Baba devotees; the Sathya Sai organisation page describes the related "Sai Ram" greeting. No Devanagari string was found on a fetched page, so script is Latin; a Devanagari form (e.g. for Hindi display) needs a source before adding. A three-word devotional phrase carries no authorship/copyright risk, but note the association differs between Shirdi Sai (d. 1918) and Sathya Sai (modern) devotees — confirm which the temple means.

title: Dvādaśa Jyotirliṅga Smaraṇam
textOriginal:
सौराष्ट्रे सोमनाथं च श्रीशैले मल्लिकार्जुनम् ।
उज्जयिन्यां महाकालमोङ्कारममलेश्वरम् ॥
परल्यां वैद्यनाथं च डाकिन्यां भीमशङ्करम् ।
सेतुबन्धे तु रामेशं नागेशं दारुकावने ॥
वाराणस्यां तु विश्वेशं त्र्यम्बकं गौतमीतटे ।
हिमालये तु केदारं घुश्मेशं च शिवालये ॥
एतानि ज्योतिर्लिङ्गानि सायं प्रातः पठेन्नरः ।
सप्तजन्मकृतं पापं स्मरणेन विनश्यति ॥
transliteration:
saurāṣṭre somanāthaṃ ca śrīśaile mallikārjunam |
ujjayinyāṃ mahākālamoṅkāramamaleśvaram ||
paralyāṃ vaidyanāthaṃ ca ḍākinyāṃ bhīmaśaṅkaram |
setubandhe tu rāmeśaṃ nāgeśaṃ dārukāvane ||
vārāṇasyāṃ tu viśveśaṃ tryambakaṃ gautamītaṭe |
himālaye tu kedāraṃ ghuśmeśaṃ ca śivālaye ||
etāni jyotirliṅgāni sāyaṃ prātaḥ paṭhennaraḥ |
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ smaraṇena vinaśyati ||
meaning: A remembrance of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna at Śrīśaila, Mahākāla at Ujjayinī, Amaleśvara at Oṃkāra, Vaidyanātha at Paralī, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, Nāgeśa in Dārukāvana, Viśveśa at Vārāṇasī, Tryambaka on the Gautamī, Kedāra in the Himālaya, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya. Whoever recites these names morning and evening is freed of the sins of seven births.
sourceText: Dvādaśa Jyotirliṅga Smaraṇam (traditional; no scriptural locus stated on the source page)

title: Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam, verse 1
textOriginal:
कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते ।
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम् ॥
transliteration:
kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate |
uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṃ daivamāhnikam ||
meaning: "Kausalyā's noble son Rāma, the eastern dawn is breaking. Arise, tiger among men; the day's sacred duties are to be done."
sourceText: Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Suprabhātam (Prativādi Bhayaṅkaram Aṇṇan, 15th c.), verse 1 — itself Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 23.2 (Viśvāmitra waking Rāma)
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). IAST generated mechanically from that Devanagari with the indic_transliteration library (Devanagari->IAST), not typed by hand; compared against checkUrl. vignanam matches word for word ("kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvāsandhyā pravartatē | uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla kartavyaṃ daivamāhnikam"); it joins "पूर्वासन्ध्या" as one word. 15th-century composition — public domain. The Rāmāyaṇa verse number (1.23.2) is the commonly cited locus and was not verified on a fetched Rāmāyaṇa page.

title: Nārāyaṇīyam 1.1
textOriginal:
सान्द्रानन्दावबोधात्मकमनुपमितं कालदेशावधिभ्यां
निर्मुक्तं नित्यमुक्तं निगमशतसहस्रेण निर्भास्यमानम् ।
अस्पष्टं दृष्टमात्रे पुनरुरुपुरुषार्थात्मकं ब्रह्मतत्त्वं
तत्तावद्भाति साक्षाद्गुरुपवनपुरे हन्त भाग्यं जनानाम् ॥
transliteration:
sāndrānandāvabodhātmakamanupamitaṃ kāladeśāvadhibhyāṃ
nirmuktaṃ nityamuktaṃ nigamaśatasahasreṇa nirbhāsyamānam |
aspaṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭamātre punarurupuruṣārthātmakaṃ brahmatattvaṃ
tattāvadbhāti sākṣādgurupavanapure hanta bhāgyaṃ janānām ||
meaning: The Absolute — dense bliss and pure awareness, beyond compare, unbounded by time and space, ever free, revealed by countless Vedic texts, yet not plainly seen — that very Brahman, the fulfilment of every human aim, shines here before us in Guruvāyūr. How fortunate are the people!
sourceText: Nārāyaṇīyam (Melpathur Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭatiri, 1586), Daśaka 1, verse 1
notes: Devanagari copied verbatim from sourceUrl (zero-width joiners and trailing verse numbers removed). title: Mīnākṣī Pañcaratnam, verse 1
textOriginal:
उद्यद्भानु सहस्रकोटिसदृशां केयूरहारोज्ज्वलां
बिम्बोष्ठीं स्मितदन्तपंक्तिरुचिरां पीताम्बरालंकृताम् ।
विष्णुब्रह्मसुरेन्द्रसेवितपदां तत्त्वस्वरूपां शिवां
मीनाक्षीं प्रणतोऽस्मि संततमहं कारुण्यवारांनिधिम् ॥
transliteration:
udyadbhānu sahasrakoṭisadṛśāṃ keyūrahārojjvalāṃ
bimboṣṭhīṃ smitadantapaṃktirucirāṃ pītāmbarālaṃkṛtām |
viṣṇubrahmasurendrasevitapadāṃ tattvasvarūpāṃ śivāṃ
mīnākṣīṃ praṇato'smi saṃtatamahaṃ kāruṇyavārāṃnidhim ||
meaning: I ever bow to Mīnākṣī, ocean of compassion — radiant like a thousand million rising suns, shining with armlets and necklaces, with lips red as bimba fruit and a lovely smile, clad in yellow silk, whose feet are served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra, the auspicious one who is the essence of truth.
sourceText: Mīnākṣī Pañcaratnam (attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya), verse 1

Source uses anusvara in पंक्ति / अलंकृताम् / संततमहं / वारांनिधिम्.

title: Jagannāthāṣṭakam, verse 1
textOriginal:
कदाचित्कालिन्दीतटविपिनसङ्गीतकरवो
मुदा गोपीनारीवदनकमलास्वादमधुपः ।
रमाशम्भुब्रह्मामरपतिगणेशार्चितपदो
जगन्नाथः स्वामी नयनपथगामी भवतु मे ॥
transliteration:
kadācitkālindītaṭavipinasaṅgītakaravo
mudā gopīnārīvadanakamalāsvādamadhupaḥ |
ramāśambhubrahmāmarapatigaṇeśārcitapado
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapathagāmī bhavatu me ||
meaning: May Lord Jagannātha become visible to my eyes — he who at times makes music in the groves on the Yamunā's bank, who like a bee joyfully tastes the lotus faces of the cowherd women, and whose feet are worshipped by Lakṣmī, Śiva, Brahmā, Indra and Gaṇeśa.
sourceText: Jagannāthāṣṭakam (attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya), verse 1

title: Kāśī Viśvanāthāṣṭakam, verse 1
textOriginal:
गङ्गातरंगरमणीयजटाकलापं
गौरीनिरन्तरविभूषितवामभागम् ।
नारायणप्रियमनंगमदापहारं
वाराणसीपुरपतिं भज विश्वनाथम् ॥
transliteration:

gaurīnirantaravibhūṣitavāmabhāgam |
nārāyaṇapriyamanaṃgamadāpahāraṃ
vārāṇasīpurapatiṃ bhaja viśvanātham ||
meaning: Worship Viśvanātha, lord of the city of Vārāṇasī — whose mass of matted hair is lovely with the Gaṅgā's waves, whose left side is ever adorned by Gaurī, beloved of Nārāyaṇa, destroyer of the pride of Kāma.
sourceText: Viśvanāthāṣṭakam (attributed to Vyāsa/Śaṅkara in tradition; no attribution on source), verse 1

title: Mūka Pañcaśatī — Āryā Śatakam, verse 1
textOriginal:
कारणपरचिद्रूपा काञ्चीपुरसीम्नि कामपीठगता ।
काचन विहरति करुणा काश्मीरस्तबककोमलाङ्गलता ॥
transliteration:
kāraṇaparacidrūpā kāñcīpurasīmni kāmapīṭhagatā |
kācana viharati karuṇā kāśmīrastabakakomalāṅgalatā ||
meaning: A certain compassion — the supreme consciousness that is the cause of all — sports within the bounds of Kāñcīpura, seated on the Kāma-pīṭha: a tender vine whose limbs are soft as clusters of saffron flowers.
sourceText: Mūka Pañcaśatī (Mūka Kavi), Āryā Śatakam, verse 1

title: Śrī Raṅganāthāṣṭakam, verse 1
textOriginal:
आनन्दरूपे निजबोधरूपे ब्रह्मस्वरूपे श्रुतिमूर्तिरूपे ।
शशाङ्करूपे रमणीयरूपे श्रीरङ्गरूपे रमतां मनो मे ॥
transliteration:
ānandarūpe nijabodharūpe brahmasvarūpe śrutimūrtirūpe |
śaśāṅkarūpe ramaṇīyarūpe śrīraṅgarūpe ramatāṃ mano me ||
meaning: May my mind delight in Śrī Raṅga's form — the form of bliss, of self-knowledge, of Brahman itself, the embodiment of the Vedas, moon-like and lovely.
sourceText: Raṅganāthāṣṭakam (attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya), verse 1
